evidence.notes: Both builds use a domain-correct queue plus case workspace, keep src/api and src/mock and all test selectors, gate actions on server allowedActions, make no mutations on load, and handle every scenario state, including draft-preserving stale recovery. Y is stronger on governed actions: its modal approve dialog shows scope, impact and the requester's reason, requires an acknowledgement and shows the receipt. Y also recomposes tables into cards on mobile, whereas X keeps desktop tables in horizontal scrollers that hide key columns at 375 and 768. X has a sturdier focus outline and cleaner component boundaries, but it fails axe color-contrast. Y's sticky internally scrolling aside and very long mobile pages are its main weaknesses. Overall Y is modestly ahead and neither build triggers a critical failure.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: At 1440 the case page is an evidence column (hypothesis, transactions, entities) with a 420px action rail (decision, freeze, audit), and the queue is sorted by severity then confidence. The AI hypothesis sits above the transaction evidence, and below 1100px the actions drop under all of the evidence.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: It has a queue plus a case workspace with evidence and an audit timeline, grouped entities with 'Why linked', 'Cited by AI · n%' badges on evidence rows, flag reasons in text and a flagged outbound total. There is no dashboard filler or chat.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: No changes under src/api or src/mock. Routes, alert-row, severity-filter, txn-row and freeze-button are kept. Actions are gated on server allowedActions (DecisionPanel `allowed = c.allowedActions.includes('record_decision')`, FreezePanel `request.allowedActions.includes('approve')`). The new tests are in a separate file and the original test is untouched. It also adds a dev-only scenario carry-over in links.ts.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: It covers loading, empty (with a clear-filters option), 503 error with retry, not-found, the read-only banner, the partial 'absence of data is not evidence of absence' banner, and stale alert scores. STALE_VERSION shows 'Reload latest version' with a vN→vM notice and keeps the draft. FORBIDDEN re-fetches allowed actions. The freeze has a review step, the receipt comes from the server, and past requests are listed.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No page overflow at any width, but tables keep a desktop layout inside overflow-x wrappers. At 375 the alert table shows only Severity, Confidence and a squeezed Alert column (Amount, Customer and the Case link are off-screen), and the transaction table shows only Time and Amount. At 768 the Location column is clipped. There are only 3 media queries.
scorer_rationale.accessibility: It has a skip link, a solid 2px :focus-visible outline on all 29 and 28 tab stops, no unnamed stops, table captions, role=meter, and a reduced-motion rule. However, axe reports serious color-contrast failures (6 nodes on the queue, 2 on the case page), and there are 14 small targets on the queue at 1440.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Calm enterprise look: a dark top bar, restrained severity colours with text labels, and consistent panels and badges. The entity grid is somewhat card-heavy but stays readable.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: It adds shared ui.tsx primitives, useResource with sequence guarding, a useAction hook that maps errors to recovery paths, and centralised format labels. Components are split per panel with a reasonable abstraction level.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: The hypothesis is labelled 'AI-generated · advisory' with a 'not evidence itself / not a probability of fraud' callout, and its basis is weighted and links to evidence. It warns when factors can't be verified or the hypothesis predates the latest case update. The freeze shows scope, impact and requester, has an inline two-step approve with the account IDs on the button, and shows the server receipt. The approval confirmation is an inline group, not a stronger acknowledgement.
